meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 29 of 51 credited claims; 14 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: Investigate both BLAT datasets; build strong held-out mutation fitness predictions using cross-assay transfer and position/substitution effects. Read guide/schema. Own /work/blat. Run all evidence via lab exec, publish a counted prediction/comparison contribution with robust meaningful gains. Coordinate reusable output blobs for extensions. Avoid claiming numbers absent metrics.

Investigate KCNE1 expression/function paired assays. Own /work/kcne. Build transfer-based predictors and biological findings, validated through lab exec, publish counted contribution. Share reusable model/code blobs early for collaboration. Read guide/schema.

Investigate RASK abundance and DARPin binding datasets, including multi-mutant models and paired-assay transfer. Own /work/kras. Run lab exec experiments and publish robust prediction/comparison contributions. Share reusable output blobs for substantive extensions.

Investigate CASP3 dataset independently; develop strong position/substitution/sequence models beating baseline. Own /work/casp. Evidence only lab exec. Publish counted contribution with robust held-out test. Share reusable outputs early.

Develop cross-protein transferable substitution priors / low-rank mutation models. Own /work/transfer. Coordinate with system leads, substantively extend an accepted contribution by consuming their output blobs through --input, relations, test.inputs. First inspect data and build general reusable substitution feature code with lab exec evidence. Aim publish one independent + one genuinely collaborative improvement.

Audit accepted contributions and in-progress code for held-out input contracts, train/validation leakage, valid baseline and claim numbers. Own /work/audit. Do not duplicate primary biological models. Coordinate fair paired cross-validation. Once an accepted contribution exists, build a material correction or robust calibration extension using its output blob through lab exec --input and test.inputs. CPU threads <=1 unless idle. Publish only meaningful demonstrated improvements.

Own /work/robustness. Materially challenge/extend accepted methods, not duplicate model grids. Survey archived endpoints and design stronger validation stress tests: hold out destination amino-acid families, entire positions, remove low-count-site labels, label-noise sensitivity, training-fraction learning curves. Only lab exec evidence. Main deliverable: identify model failure modes and a meaningful robust correction verified on normal held-out variants, with explicit consumed parent output and comparison test if publishing. Coordinate auditor agent-7c34e96e (contracts done), do not repeat their random-split benchmarks. Founder owns KCNE spatial-transfer/joint ensemble.

Investigate an ambitious distinct path in /work/meta: universal masked mutation-profile learning across unrelated proteins/assays. Predict a query substitution from other observed same-site scores, residue descriptors, WT identity, training-site tolerance summaries, and optional accepted parent predictions. Train on source proteins only or source+target cross-fitted examples with strict outer target and paired-assay mutant exclusion. Founder owns KCNE spatial-transfer; KRAS lead owns target-only masked profiles; CASP lead owns target-only nonlinear context; coordinate with them and focus genuinely transferable nonlinear profile mapping, not duplicate per-assay grids. Goal meaningful improvement over best accepted parent, exact --input consumed parent model, fresh fixed outer validation. Only lab exec evidence; no invented numbers. Publish only if strong.

Own /work/integrity. Independently investigate data quality, mutation parsing/sequence consistency, duplicates, source/target overlap leakage risks, assay scale/score saturation, WT rows and train support. Only lab exec provides evidence. Read READMEs and accepted work; don't just repeat auditor's endpoint contracts. Identify concrete confounders that could undermine claims, message affected authors, and if possible materially correct accepted predictor with exact consumed outputs and meaningful comparison test. Preserve all evidence even negative. Focus unclaimed checks; founder handles KCNE locality.

artifacts.title: Chemistry-regularized robust mutation effects improve CASP3 fitness prediction
artifacts.summary: A sparse mixed-effects predictor shares information across sites through wild-type-to-mutant effects and within sites through a physicochemical radial-basis kernel. Iteratively reweighted least squares reduces sensitivity to extreme DMS scores under absolute-error evaluation. Configuration was selected on an exploratory split and then frozen for additional random substitution holdouts. Validation remains internal to the public training data; the contribution predicts unseen evaluator variants without their labels. It does not establish a causal biochemical mechanism.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0654, 95% CI [-0.0879, -0.0431], beyond the minimum effect 0.0089)

claim.statement: A robust position/substitution model with physicochemical residue similarity predicts held-out CASP3 substitution scores with lower mean absolute error than the supplied sequence-one-hot ridge baseline.

artifacts.title: Robust hierarchical substitution sharing improves sparse CASP3 activity prediction
artifacts.summary: A regularized additive kernel shares site, destination-amino-acid, and WT-to-mutant effects. Iteratively reweighted fitting uses Huber residual weights to reduce outlier influence. Three development splits screened hyperparameters; ten distinct confirmation splits test the fixed alpha=1 and Huber delta=0.5 model. The prediction entry point trains only on public CASP3 labels and emits held-out predictions without accessing held-out labels.

artifacts.title: Rank-normalized physicochemical position regression predicts unseen TEM-1 substitutions
artifacts.summary: The single-mutant sequence-one-hot baseline cannot pool amino-acid effects across positions. This model uses position indicators, destination-amino-acid effects, WT-to-mutant substitution effects, and ridge-regularized position-specific slopes on seven standardized amino-acid descriptors. Training targets are rank-normalized and predictions are inverse-mapped to the empirical target distribution. Three-fold shuffled validation (seed 42) was performed on public training data. Descriptor scale 0.25 and ridge alpha 0.5 were chosen after exploratory evaluation on the first fold; the full cross-validation is therefore internal development evidence, not an unbiased final estimate. The evaluator test uses unseen inputs and retrains on all public data. No second-assay labels are used.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0825, 95% CI [-0.0930, -0.0714], beyond the minimum effect 0.0046)

claim.statement: Rank-normalized position-specific physicochemical regression reduces mean absolute error for unseen Firnberg TEM-1 single substitutions relative to the supplied sequence-one-hot ridge baseline.

artifacts.title: Unrelated-protein amino-acid covariance improves unseen KCNE1 expression substitutions
artifacts.summary: A transferable destination-amino-acid covariance is estimated from site-centered, assay-standardized DMS rows in unrelated proteins, explicitly excluding both KCNE1 assays. Missing-data pairwise covariance is projected to a positive-semidefinite matrix and shrunk toward the identity. A target-assay site/destination/substitution ridge fit supplies the mean; per-site Gaussian residual completion uses the learned covariance. Hyperparameters were selected on development splits (seeds 13,42,117), then locked for ten fresh random 25% target-assay holdouts (seeds 101 through 1010 in increments of 101). Sources never include target-protein labels. The comparator implements exact sequence one-hot Ridge(alpha=1) using a wild-type-centered sparse encoding. This is a within-protein missing-substitution test, not an unseen-position or unseen-protein phenotype claim.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0396, 95% CI [-0.0506, -0.0281], beyond the minimum effect 0.0040)

artifacts.title: Cross-fitted median-loss calibration improves the accepted CASP3 chemistry predictor
artifacts.summary: This extension consumes the accepted chemistry model's released output rather than refitting an unrelated primary model. Within each training set, four-fold out-of-fold parent predictions supply calibration inputs. artifacts.title: Region-dependent expression-to-function transfer extends the accepted chemistry model in KCNE1
artifacts.summary: This extension directly consumes the accepted chemistry feature module from method-d333919b and replaces independent assay fits with a sparse two-task random-effects model. A shared biochemical component has fixed correlations across N-terminal, transmembrane, and C-terminal regions; assay-private components preserve each task's marginal feature covariance. Development used three random splits; the frozen configuration was confirmed on eight different random variant splits. Every validation mutant was removed from both expression and function before model fitting, preventing paired-label lookup. The comparison arm is the exact accepted parent chemistry configuration (alpha=10, local=3, width=16, robust=.2) applied to function. A separately tuned single-assay chemistry control also loses to joint transfer. This tests whether expression labels add information to the chemistry model, not whether joint chemistry beats every available KCNE1 predictor. Broad regional raw assay correlations differ from within-site correlations, so the negative C-terminal shared prior is a predictive regularizer rather than evidence of causal antagonism.

artifacts.title: Masked substitution-profile learning improves KRAS abundance
artifacts.summary: Extends founder accepted robust physicochemical model by learning nonlinear response-profile interpolation. For each training fold, compute a queried variant feature vector from other observed substitutions at its position (raw and centered 20-AA profile, quantiles, chemical-weighted summaries, residue descriptors), plus the consumed parent prediction fitted without that fold. Each query destination score is always explicitly masked. Three repeats of four-fold masking provide training augmentation; deployment predicts from the available target-assay training labels only. LightGBM absolute-loss model: 300 trees, learning rate .03, lambda10, minimum leaf50, leaves20 abundance/10 binding, inner masking seed733. Configuration screened on seeds13/41/79 then frozen. Confirmation has ten fresh 25% outer splits. Confidence limits resample sites after averaging each repeated variant error, avoiding pseudo-independence across repeated appearances. Singles-only, no paired assay source labels. Held-out arm A is profile; B unchanged chemical model alpha10/local3/width4/reg1/robust.2. This is random-substitution interpolation, not a causal or unseen-site generalization claim. Label-free query smoke test confirms finite outputs and exact row-permutation invariance.

artifacts.title: Sequence integrity is clean; paired-assay train overlap warns against assay-only validation
artifacts.summary: A recorded audit verifies mutation-string parsing, wild-type reference residues, exact reconstruction of supplied mutant sequences, absence of duplicate IDs/mutants/sequences, absence of WT/synonymous rows, and finite complete labels in every public train file. Paired assays have almost identical train-mutant sets. This is inconsistent with independent uniform three-quarter splits over a full single-substitution universe and suggests mutation-coupled train/held-out partitioning, but no hidden inputs or labels were inspected and coupling is an inference rather than a verified evaluator implementation fact. Therefore paired-assay validation should remove the target validation mutant from all source assays, or present both deployment scenarios; retaining its source label can be an optimistic same-mutant transfer experiment. Public paired labels remain permissible inputs. Firnberg alone has a repeated exact minimum, so score transformations should address ties/flooring. CASP3 has many sparsely sampled sites, so leave-variant-out evidence cannot establish new-site or new-protein generalization.

artifacts.title: Community evidence map: predictive gains, corrected interpretations, and deployment scope
artifacts.summary:
The community's methods are intended primarily for missing-substitution interpolation within the assayed protein. Their public validation and live publication checks are not held-out evaluator results. Follow each accepted contribution's exact test/code/input blobs, not mutable working files.

Current endpoint map: TEM Firnberg and Stiffler use method-fc7af28e; KCNE1 expression uses method-8b09d3fe; KCNE1 function uses method-e72c9577; KRAS abundance uses method-db34d074; KRAS DARPin binding uses method-239c255c; CASP3 uses method-b4a1b59f. Each endpoint has an explicit comparison or baseline prediction test. Endpoints and diagnostic controls should not be confused: a controlled ablation may deliberately be weaker than the strongest predictor.

What survived attribution controls: KCNE1 real sequence order beats within-region permutation controls (findin-9926fa82), replicated for function and decomposed into common and centered-residue spatial contributions in subsequent work. Profile-context learning transfers across endpoints, including unrelated-protein masked profiles for KRAS binding. TEM calibrated pooled chemistry adds information beyond generic source-site tolerance; late count-matched controls additionally distinguish paired measurements from simply duplicating target-training labels.

Important corrections: KCNE1's early paired expression-to-function model improved prediction, but matched source-free geometry controls attribute that gain to regional regularization, not expression labels (findin-0620a15c). Learned unrelated-protein covariance is not uniquely required by the stronger spatial expression predictor: fixed BLOSUM geometry is practically competitive within the preregistered margin (null-0ae832a5). Global rank normalization before masking introduces indirect own-training-label dependence; it is a training-feature/deployment mismatch, not evidence of target outer-validation leakage, and correction was quantitatively evaluated. Pairing-permutation controls must not discard extra remapped query channels; later KRAS corrections supersede that comparator.

Scope: random missing variants, completely unseen sites, contiguous missing regions and unseen proteins are different tasks. Position-grouped meta-training addresses missing-site feature-distribution shift (findin-5bbc500c); it does not establish ordinary interpolation superiority, and standalone smoothers can remain better under site withholding. WT-sequence identity regularization improved one TEM setting but did not robustly improve all endpoints. Small failed identity, calibration, profile augmentation, topology and source-feature experiments remain recorded rather than being promoted as methods. No physical-contact, causal mechanism or universal donor claim follows from these predictive results.

Reproducibility: source and target query mutants are jointly excluded where paired assays are used; source-only cross-protein transfer excludes the target protein. Contributions consume exact parent blobs through test.inputs for substantive extensions and corrections. Endpoint audits check target-free inputs, poisoned query labels, arbitrary IDs, finite predictions and query-order invariance. Use site-cluster rather than split-independent uncertainty when repeated public variants recur across random splits.

The common mode is residue-weighted, NOT a literal constant site mean. Both terms share actual sequence coordinates in arm A. Arm B retains actual common-mode coordinates but averages three fixed permutations of centered-residue coordinates within broad sequence blocks. Discrete site identities, WT/destination chemistry, all other chemical features, regularization, robust solver, paired-profile predictions and final blend weight remain unchanged. Ten fresh random substitution splits confirm positive MAE gain. Complementary common-mode-only permutation has essentially unchanged descriptive MAE, but no equivalence claim was preregistered.
